lines.text: Your next phone may have less memory.
TrendForce says budget phones are settling around four gigabytes, mid-range back to eight.
Why? Memory makers are serving AI servers first.
Server memory was expected to jump about 90% in one quarter.
Phone memory got pricier too, so makers are cutting gigabytes.
And the squeeze is expected to last into 2027.
Buying a phone, in India or anywhere? Check the RAM first.

post.title: Your next phone may have less memory
post.caption:
Your next phone may have LESS memory 📉📱 and AI is the reason.

Memory makers are putting AI servers first. TrendForce (5 Jan 2026) says suppliers are prioritising server applications, which limits supply for everything else; on 2 Feb 2026 it expected server DRAM contract prices to rise about 90% in a single quarter (1Q26), the biggest jump on record, with phone memory (LPDDR4X and LPDDR5X) up about 90% too.

Phones are paying for it. TrendForce (14 May 2026): high-end phones settle on 12GB as 16GB fades, mid-range reverts to 8GB, and entry-level models mostly settle around 4GB. In July it said a server DRAM shortage is already expected for 2027.

Buying a phone soon, in India or anywhere? Check the RAM before the price. How much RAM is in yours? 👇 Send this to the friend who's about to buy one.

sources.note: TrendForce, 14 May 2026, Mobile DRAM Contract Prices Continue Rising in 2Q26 (read 22 Nov 2026): 'In the high-end segment, 12GB is becoming the mainstream configuration while 16GB adoption declines. Meanwhile, mid-range devices are reverting to 8GB as the core specification, and entry-level models mostly settle around 4GB.' LPDDR4X ASP +70-75% QoQ, LPDDR5X +78-83% QoQ in 2Q26.

TrendForce, 5 Jan 2026, Memory Makers Prioritize Server Applications, Driving Across-the-Board Price Increases in 1Q26 (read 22 Nov 2026): 'This shift has significantly limited supply in other markets'; 'The global server market is expected to reach its peak in 2026 as North American CSPs speed up investments in AI infrastructure.'

TrendForce, 2 Feb 2026, Memory Price Outlook for 1Q26 Sharply Upgraded (read 22 Nov 2026): 'Intense competition among buyers for the limited supply is expected to drive server DRAM prices up by around 90% QoQ in 1Q26, marking the largest quarterly increase on record.' 'Contract prices for LPDDR4X and LPDDR5X are both expected to surge by around 90% QoQ in 1Q26.'

TrendForce, 9 Jul 2026, Server DRAM Contract Prices Expected to Rise 13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 (read 22 Nov 2026): 'Meanwhile, a server DRAM shortage is already anticipated for 2027.' Also 30 Sep 2026 (20260930-13258): 'DRAM supply will remain tight in 2027.'
